name: Chat storage: folder layout (git-compatible, O(message) writes)
description:
## Objective
Replace the "one giant JSON per chat" storage with a **chat = folder** layout so that chat/task storage is git-compatible, reviewable, and O(message) instead of O(whole chat) per write. Design is complete below — implement it in the P0 → P1 → P2 order. **Do not compress or hide conversations in a database**: the source of truth must stay plain files in the repo.

## Measured evidence (live project, `.codx/tasks`)
- 1810 chat files, 334.6 MB, 1896 files tracked by git, `.git` = 160 MB.
- Worst chat: 18 messages, **14.05 MB**, of which **13.81 MB (98.3 %) is `tool_events`**; content is 83 KB. gzip → 2.48 MB (5.7×).
- 4th case: 2 messages, 6.91 MB — a single giant paste.
- Write path: `ChatManager._persist_chat_messages` → `save_chat` → `store_chat` = `model_dump` → `json.dumps(indent=2)` → `flush` → `fsync` → `os.replace`, i.e. a **full read-merge-rewrite of the whole file**, triggered by **every tool event** (start and end) via `chat_event_bridge._persist_message`; only streaming is throttled (5 s).
- ⇒ one turn (~40 tool calls) on the worst chat ≈ **1.1 GB of I/O for 90 KB of conversation**. This is the disk saturation behind "the client waits".
- Board listing (`list_chats` → `load_chat_from_path(chat_only=True)`) still **parses all 1810 files**; `chat_only` does not skip tool events.
- Attachments are base64 **inside** the chat JSON (`ChatAttachment.base64_data`, `db.py:47`), so a screenshot adds +33 % to the file that is rewritten every event.
- **2 task files are already corrupt** ("Extra data"): `.codx/tasks/codx-junior maintenance/Backlog/ui-updates.04312e27-….json` (4199 trailing bytes) and `…/In progress/github-integration-foundation-settings-client-endpoints.409bee26-….json` (39185 trailing bytes). `list_chats` swallows `ValueError`, so those tasks silently vanished from the board — the failure mode of whole-file rewrites.

## Key design rule
gzip ratios (2.4–5.7×) are what **git already does to every blob**, so compressing files inside the working tree buys nothing in the repo and costs the diff:
> **Compress what humans never review** (tool events, cold tasks, giant pastes). **Keep what humans review** (messages, metadata) as plain text and let git compress.

## Target layout
```
.codx/tasks/<board>/<column>/<slug>.<chat_id>/
  chat.json                     # 1–3 KB, TRACKED (id, name, board, column, status, cost,
                                #   timestamps, root_id, message_count, storage hints)
  messages/
    0001-user-<doc_id>.md       # TRACKED — frontmatter + content verbatim
    0002-assistant-<doc_id>.md
  attachments/
    a1b2c3d4e5f6-screenshot.png # TRACKED (content-addressed → dedupes identical pastes)
  events/                       # NOT TRACKED (data plane, like .codx/chat_turns)
    0002-assistant-<doc_id>.tool-events.jsonl
    0002-assistant-<doc_id>.phases.jsonl
```

### Message file
```
---
doc_id: 6735da2e-2df0-4ac3-a989-361159677eb3
role: assistant
created_at: 2026-11-15T12:14:59.123
updated_at: 2026-11-15T12:16:02.001
done: true
model: codx-junior
cost: 0.0312
read_by: [alice]
usage: {prompt_tokens: 1200, completion_tokens: 340}
tools: 7                      # count only — payload lives in events/
events: events/0002-assistant-<doc_id>.tool-events.jsonl
---

The answer, as markdown, verbatim.
```
- `content` stays markdown → readable in the editor, on GitHub, in `git diff`.
- `think` goes in a trailing `<details><summary>Thinking</summary>` block (collapsed, still diffable).
- `tool_events` / `phase_events` / `lifecycle_events` **never** enter this file, only their count.
- Content > 128 KB → body becomes a ~2 KB preview + pointer, payload in `attachments/<doc_id>.md.gz`.
- Frontmatter parsed up to the **first** lone `---`, so `---` in the body is harmless.

### Event logs (append-only)
One JSON object per line: at tool start `{"id":…,"tool":…,"status":"running"}`, at end a second line with the result (`response` 4 KB head + tail, `output` capped, full text → `events/<doc_id>.tool-<call_id>.out.gz`). Readers keep the last line per `tool_call_id`. No read-modify-write, crash safe, and a torn tail costs one event instead of the whole task.

## Why it is fast
| operation | today | after |
|---|---|---|
| append user message | read+parse+dump 14 MB | create ~2 KB file + 1 KB `chat.json` |
| tool event | read+parse+dump+fsync entire chat | append ~1 line to a jsonl |
| streaming flush | rewrite 14 MB | rewrite 1 message file (debounced 2 s) |
| board listing (1810 chats) | parse 334 MB | read 1810 × ~1 KB ≈ 1.8 MB |
| open one chat | 14 MB | ~90 KB (18 message files) |
| full-text search | Python parses 334 MB | `rg --json messages/` in `asyncio.to_thread` |
| I/O per turn (worst chat) | ~1.1 GB | < 2 MB |

Git history becomes O(total content) instead of O(turns × chat size).

## Storage policy (`.codx/storage.json`, per project/board)
| mode | tracked | compressed | when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plain` (default) | chat.json + messages/ + attachments/ | no | boards you review |
| `events-gzip` | same | `events/*.jsonl.gz` after the turn (last 3 turns plain) | default for agent work |
| `cold-archive` | only an `index.json` entry | chat folder → `tasks/.archive/<id>.tar.gz` via the existing `TaskArchive` (`kanban/archive.py`) after N days in a `done` column | finished sprints |
| `attachments: track\|ignore\|lfs` | — | — | screenshots vs source |

`events/` untracked by default, consistent with the existing data-plane `.gitignore` policy (`chat_turns`, `browser_sessions`). Every artifact stays `cat`/`rg`/`git diff`-able; the only binary form is the cold tar.gz that `TaskArchive` already restores byte-for-byte.

### Optional derived index (only if needed later)
If listing/search is still slow at 5000 chats, add **SQLite in WAL mode under `.codx/db/` as a rebuildable cache** — never source of truth: rows from `chat.json`, FTS5 from `messages/*.md`, invalidated by `(mtime_ns,size)`. Deleting the file loses nothing.

## Implementation plan (each step independently shippable)
**P0 — stop the bleeding, no format change**
1. Cap `ToolEvent.output`/`response` at write time (4 KB head + 1 KB tail), full text to an untracked sidecar → 14 MB → ~0.3 MB.
2. Debounce assistant-message persist (1–2 s); `fsync` only at terminal boundaries (turn end, user message, cancel).
3. Keep an authoritative in-process chat; re-read from disk only when `(mtime,size)` changed (reuse `_CHAT_INFO_CACHE` in `chat_manager.py`).
4. Repair the 2 corrupt files and log dropped chats instead of swallowing `ValueError` in `list_chats`.

**P1 — folder layout**
5. `get_chat_dir` + folder reader/writer; `chat.json` metadata; message `.md` files; sequence-prefixed names under a per-chat `flock` (pattern already in `TaskArchive.locked()` and `turn_store.py`).
6. `load_chat(chat_only=True)` reads **only** `chat.json` → board listing stops parsing payloads.
7. Attachments → `attachments/<sha256>-<name>` + reference; drop `base64_data` from the persisted model (keep accepting it at the API boundary).
8. Compat reader: a chat is *either* `<slug>.<id>.json` (legacy) *or* a folder; migrate lazily on next write + a one-shot `migrate-tasks` command run as a single commit.
9. Lazy timeline endpoint `GET /chats/{id}/messages/{doc_id}/events`.

**P2 — policy & cold storage**
10. `storage.json` policy; auto `cold-archive` of `done` boards; event retention (full events for last K turns, then counts + errors only).
11. Search through ripgrep; optionally the SQLite derived index.

## Acceptance criteria
- A chat folder round-trips to the same `Chat` model (all fields) and back.
- Writing one message of a 19-message / 8 MB legacy chat touches < 100 KB on disk (measured with `strace`/IO counters or by comparing bytes written).
- `list_chats` on a 1800-chat fixture reads only `chat.json` files; its latency becomes a regression test.
- Concurrent appends to the same chat never produce a partially written file; a torn jsonl tail is recovered (one lost event).
- Legacy `<slug>.<id>.json` chats are still readable before and after lazy migration; migration is idempotent.
- `rg` finds text in `messages/*.md`; `git diff` of a new message is one added file (+ unchanged `chat.json` timestamps only).
- The 2 corrupt task files are recovered or explicitly quarantined with a log line, not silently dropped.

## Explicitly NOT in scope
- No database as source of truth (breaks review, `git merge`, and the "no hidden sensitive data" requirement).
- No gzip on tracked message files (git already compresses; you would only lose the diff).
- No JSONL for the conversation body (streaming turns it into an append storm that grows with tokens).
- No reformatting `chat.json` to compact JSON once it holds only metadata.

## Notes
- Related work already on disk (separate workstream, do not duplicate): `conversation_response` in `db.py` strips unsent drafts, `client/src/store/chats.js` merge fixes, atomic `os.replace` write + `_CHAT_INFO_CACHE` in `chat_manager.py`.
